tools.name: bursia_status
tools.description: Use when you need Burs-IA's own current operational status (interfaces, Utils door). Not a capability list (discover_capabilities) and not policy (human_oversight_policy).

tools.name: discover_capabilities
tools.description: Use when you want to know which of Burs-IA's OWN capabilities fit a need (browse). For external services use ruta; to classify one concrete request into a lane use capability_triage; to check a known MCP URL use bursia_verify_mcp. Read-only.

tools.name: capability_triage
tools.description: Use when you already have ONE concrete request and want to know which Burs-IA lane would handle it. Classification only: nothing runs. To browse capabilities use discover_capabilities; to do it in one call use resolver.

tools.name: agent_collaboration_request
tools.description: Use when another AI agent should collaborate with you. Prepares and classifies the request only; nothing is sent. If a human must approve, use human_bridge_request; for an invitation draft to one known HTTPS target, prepare_outbound_invitation.

tools.name: human_bridge_request
tools.description: Use when a person must review or approve a bounded request before anything happens. Prepares the handoff only; contacts nobody. For agent-to-agent use agent_collaboration_request.

tools.name: human_oversight_policy
tools.description: Read Burs-IA rules for autonomy, human oversight, revocation and consequential-action gates; see outbound_gateway_policy, bursia_status.

tools.name: outbound_gateway_policy
tools.description: Read the exact outbound communication and external-send policy; prepare_outbound_invitation only prepares, sends stay human-authorized.

tools.name: prepare_outbound_invitation
tools.description: Use when you have one specific public HTTPS target and want a ready-to-review invitation draft. It is never sent; sending stays human-authorized (see outbound_gateway_policy). For a general agent-to-agent need use agent_collaboration_request.

tools.name: bursia_worknet_paid_tasks
tools.description: List paid WORKNET opportunities (public-safe metadata only); does not apply, claim, accept, spend or contact.

tools.name: bursia_worknet_task
tools.description: Read the public-safe canonical record of one paid WORKNET opportunity by id (WN-NNN).

tools.name: bursia_worknet_prepare_mission
tools.description: Deterministic internal pre-contract mission preview for one paid WORKNET item; no external write, claim, payment or contact.

tools.name: bursia_verify_mcp
tools.description: Use when you have a specific public MCP endpoint URL and want a detailed read-only verification report with evidence. No target tool runs, no credentials; not a security certification. To find servers use ruta; for what our explorer already saw about a registry host, bursia_eco.

tools.name: bursia_eco
tools.description: Use when you want the stored observation of one MCP-registry host by Burs-IA's explorer, layer by layer, with zero-cost fixes. Pull only; nobody is contacted; null = not measured. For a fresh live check use bursia_verify_mcp.

tools.name: resolver
tools.description: Use when you want Burs-IA to handle one public request end to end in a single call: verify an MCP endpoint or answer a question about real Burs-IA capabilities, returning status and a receipt. findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "bursia_verify_mcp" references sensitive artifacts (credentials). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "reputacion" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Use when you want to know what is publicly known about ONE AI/agent service before using or paying it. Pass its domain and get Burs-IA's public record: what its…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: ruta, discover_capabilities, bursia_verify_mcp, datos_abiertos · Private data: human_bridge_request, bursia_worknet_paid_tasks, bursia_worknet_task, bursia_worknet_prepare_mission, bursia_verify_mcp, reputacion, empresa · Public sink: outbound_gateway_policy.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: ruta, discover_capabilities, bursia_verify_mcp, datos_abiertos · Private data: human_bridge_request, bursia_worknet_paid_tasks, bursia_worknet_task, bursia_worknet_prepare_mission, bursia_verify_mcp, reputacion, empresa · Public sink: outbound_gateway_policy

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "bursia_status" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Overall Burs-IA status. Capabilities: discover_capabilities. Autonomy: human_oversight_policy. Send rules: outbound_gateway_policy." → after: "Use when you need Burs-IA's own current operational status (interfaces, Utils door). Not a capability list (discover_capabilities) and not policy (human_oversight_policy)."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
